title: fix: cuda-graph shape-guard warmup regression causing incorrect replay for variable batch sizes
author: Priya Raman
description:
Summary:

This PR fixes a regression in the CUDA graph capture/replay warmup path where shape-guarded graphs were replayed with stale kernel launch parameters when the batch dimension changed between warmup and production runs. The bug caused incorrect memory offsets for KV cache slices and, in some cases, a kernel launch with mismatched grid/block configuration leading to soft failures observed as corrupted outputs or occasional device asserts in intensive workloads.

Root cause:
- The shape guard metadata attached to a captured graph was not fully normalizing dynamic dims for the KV cache offset calculation. During warmup we were capturing graphs using exemplar inputs; when the live request had a different batch size the replay path reused kernel parameter state that depended on the warmup tensor strides.
- A prior change (ENG-4321) introduced an optimization to avoid re-computing per-replay offsets for a narrow set of shapes; that optimization had an edge-case for batch dimension != warmup_batch which surfaced under multi-client continuous batching.

What this change does:
- Normalize dynamic dimensions used by the shape guard metadata at capture time and store an explicit per-graph "replay-normalization" vector that the replay path applies before computing KV cache offsets and launch configs.
- Force recomputation of grid/block and shared-memory footprint when batch dimension differs from the warmup exemplar. This is gated to the minimal set of cases to avoid perf regressions for the common equal-shape path.
- Adds an integration test to the runtime CI that exercises capture->replay across a range of batch sizes and continuous-batching scenarios to prevent regressions.
- Adds a short doc section describing the shape guard invariants and the warmup recommendations for model owners.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests covering shape guard normalization and offset recompute added.
- CI integration test (cpu/gpu matrix) added to catch replay mismatches for batch sizes 1..8.
- Internal perf benchmarks show no measurable degradation for same-shape replay; end-to-end latency for a 16-token request with batch=4 changed by +0.2% (within noise); regression fixes eliminate the 0.5-1.5% error-rate seen in affected workloads.

Related tickets and background:
- Linked Linear: ENG-4321 (root cause investigation and perf delta analysis)
- Related PRs: pr-19458, pr-20322, pr-21034 that iterated on shape-guard warmup behavior.

Backwards compatibility:
- This change is backward compatible; older graphs will have the normalization vector computed on first replay and cached. There is a small one-time replay cost for previously captured graphs but no correctness breakage.

Checklist:
- [x] Repro case added to internal test harness
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Perf validation on benchmark-lab
- [x] Docs updated
